entries.title: Proverbs 20:1
segments: Since wine and strong drink darken the reason, bring the soul under the control of excitement and passion, and thus prepare it for folly and wickedness of every sort, no wise man will give himself up to their power.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:2
segments: Fear of a king; his wrath, which is an object of fear to his subjects.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:3
segments: Meddling; embroiling himself in contentions.  But we may better render, "Every fool will be angry;" that is, by giving way to a passionate spirit, will involve himself in strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:5
segments: Man; that is, a wise man; his heart is an inexhaustible reservoir of knowledge, from which the skilful can draw at all times.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:6
segments: They who make the largest professions of goodness and love, are in general the least worthy of confidence in any work that requires patient and self-denying toil.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:7
segments: The best inheritance which a man can leave to his children is his own holy life.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:8
segments: With his eyes; by his vigilance and sagacity in detecting iniquity.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:9
segments: The best men are most deeply conscious of their sinfulness.  It is only the blinding power of sin that leads any to claim that they are free from it.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:12
segments: The Lord hath made even both of them; "He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? he that formed the eye, shall he not see?"

entries.title: Proverbs 20:14
segments:
Naught; that is, bad in quality. 
 
  Boasteth; of his good bargain. 
 
The habit of buyers to depreciate, and of sellers to exaggerate the worth of articles of traffic, is a species of dishonesty as base and degrading as it is common.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:15
segments: Gold, and a multitude of rubies--a precious jewel; gold and precious gems are comparatively plenty, but the lips of knowledge are a much rarer and more valuable possession.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:16
segments:
Take his garment--a stranger; as much as to say, If one is so foolish as to become a surety for a stranger, he will have to pledge his garment to you for money to meet the obligation thus incurred; and you will have to take his garment, for he will be unable to redeem it himself. 
 
  Take a pledge--strange woman; nothing better can be expected of the same foolish man, than that he should pledge his garment to you for money to be used by him as the hire of a strange woman, and with the same result as before.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:17
segments:
Shall be filled with gravel; the bread will, as it were, turn to gravel in his mouth; his fraud will end in sorrow. 
 
It is only in anticipation that dishonest gain is pleasant; its end is bitterness and vexation of spirit.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:19
segments:
Flattereth with his lips; literally, openeth wide his lips, that is, as a talebearer, for he will reveal your secrets also. 
 
The man who reveals to us the secrets of others, proves himself unworthy to be intrusted with our own.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:20
segments: God returns the injurious conduct of children upon their own heads. Filial ingratitude is the direct road to ruin, temporal and spiritual.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:21
segments: Gotten hastily; that is, more hastily than it could have been by righteous means.
As "he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent," so neither shall his prosperity be permanent.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:22
segments: We always do well to leave vengeance in the hands of God, to whom it belongs.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:25
segments:
Who devoureth that which is holy; appropriates to his own use that which, by the law, should have been consecrated to God's service.  But it may be rendered, who rashly makes vows of consecration. 
 
  To make inquiry; whether they shall be kept. 
 
Rash vows, by which men bind themselves to certain outward actions under the name of religion, are highly perniciuos in their influence. When the young and inexperienced take upon themselves vows of celibacy and exclusion from society, they only spread a snare for their souls.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:26
segments: Bringeth the wheel; of the threshing-wagon; that is, he destroys them.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:27
segments:
The candle of the Lord; a candle which God has placed within him. 
 
  Searching all the inward parts; taking cognizance of his most secret thoughts.

entries.title: Proverbs 20:30
segments:
Blueness; the reference is to the scars made by severe blows.  We may paraphrase the verse thus: Severe blows inflicted upon the transgressor cleanse his soul from evil; and stripes, his inward spirit. 
 
That chastisement which cleanses the soul from sin is a rich blessing, however severe it may be.
